# W5-KR1 — Group-complexity jump: the wall is a +1 in the Eilenberg hierarchy   ·   VERDICT: KILLED

**Card claim:** #G(M_<=r)=0 (aperiodic) for r<=60 and increments at 61 — the reversible rounds are the flip-flop part, the feed-forward collision the group part; the first round whose round-transformation monoid contains a nontrivial group element is predicted to be r=61.

**Probe run:** N=2,3 (throttled). For each round r=55..63 built the transformation monoid generated by the round head-map { (a,e) -> SHA_round_head(state, K[r], w) } over ALL message words w (the card's "over all W[r]"), carrier = all (a,e) head pairs with tail lanes pinned, closed under composition, and detected the first round with a nontrivial group element (an element of functional period > 1). The round OPERATION is identical for all r; only k=K[r]&mask changes.

**Result (numbers):**
- N=2 (carrier 16 states, monoid fully enumerated, |M|=36864): a nontrivial group element with **max functional period 12** is present at **r=55** — the earliest round tested — and IDENTICALLY at every round 55..63 (same |M|=36864, same period 12). First group round = **55**, NOT 61.
- N=3 (carrier 64 states): the monoid exceeds the 200001 cap at EVERY round 55..63 (uniformly) — INCONCLUSIVE at N=3, but uniform across rounds, so no round-61 jump is possible.

**Kill_criterion:** "group element appears at r<=58." — **fired? YES** (group element at r=55).

**Verdict reasoning:** The kill fires emphatically: a nontrivial group element appears at r=55 (≤58), the earliest round probed, and is present unchanged at every round through 63. There is no aperiodic-below-60 / group-at-61 increment. The reason is structural: the SHA round update is a BIJECTION on the interior state given the message word (it can be inverted round-by-round), so the round map is a permutation of finite order — i.e. a group element — at every single round; an additive round constant K[r] cannot change that. The "+1 in the Eilenberg hierarchy at the wall" is bookkeeping: the rounds are NOT the flip-flop (aperiodic) part — they are reversible permutations (already group-bearing). The genuine non-group-bearing / collision step is the final feed-forward ADD (IV + tail), which is many-to-one and lives OUTSIDE the round monoid (see W5-KR5). This is prior finding #4 (no round-60 knee): group complexity is round-invariant, not localized to round 61.

**Cross-check / skeptic note:** Could the head-carrier (pinning tail lanes b,c,d,f,g,h to a constant) fabricate a group that the full state lacks? No — restricting to a sub-coordinate can only QUOTIENT/divide the monoid, and a group quotient of an aperiodic monoid is trivial; observing period-12 elements proves genuine group complexity is present. Independent corroboration: W5-KR3's aperiodicity probe shows the SAME round-invariance (its verdict is byte-identical for r=57..61). Both converge on: nothing algebraically special happens at 60->61.

**Reproduce:** `OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 taskpolicy -b python3 wild_angles/probes/cards/W5-KR1.py`
